atoms.sound: Who was the Queen of England before Elizabuth the first?

feedback.end: While Mary I was queen, she tried to make England follow Catholicism — a different type of Christianity. Her violence towards Protestants during this time earned her the nickname Bloody Mary!

instruction.text: Find the cross in the picture.

end.text: Although Mary tried to make England a Catholic country, Elizabeth was a Protestant. When she became queen, she returned the country to Protestantism.

instruction.text: One of Elizabeth’s biggest successes was defeating Spain’s attempt to invade England. Select the Spanish ship to learn more.

atoms.text: This is King Philip II of Spain, Elizabeth’s enemy. In 1588, he sent a group of ships, also known as the Spanish Armada, to invade England.

instruction.text: Elizabeth sent more than 100 ships to fight back! Select her to hear what she said to the English troops.

atoms.sound: I have the heart and stomach of a king. We shall shortly have a famous victory over these enemies.

atoms.text: The Spanish troops were forced to retreat and England won.

instruction.text: You’re talking to a historian about Queen Elizabeth I. Fill in the gaps.
instruction.sound: You’re talking to a historian about Queen Elizabeth the first. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: It seems like Queen Elizabeth I was a very ((++good annoying)) queen. Did everyone love her?
By the end of her reign, Queen Elizabeth I was very ((++popular funny)), but, at the beginning, some people did not like her.
In Tudor times, women were expected to ((++get_married have_fun)) and have children, but Elizabeth never did.
Lots of people thought she would be a ((++bad brilliant)) ruler without a man’s help and were angry that she had no children to be ((++heir hare)) to the throne.
Wow, it seems like it was very ((++hard easy)) for a woman to be queen in Tudor times! How did Elizabeth make people like her in the end?
Elizabeth showed people how committed she was to her role as ((++Queen King)) of England. Instead of finding a husband, Elizabeth said that she was married to England.
